Interesting Facebook discussion that I figured I'd post on here. A man who I was told works in the Arizona Libertarian party was saying that believing in the NAP was not a requirement to be considered Libertarian.

I wanted to get more opinions so I figured I'd ask it on here. The NAP to me is paramount to my belief in libertarianism but his point was that many early libertarians were more utilitarian than non-aggressive and that while he believed in the NAP, he didn't think it defined the belief/party.

What say you? Is there a way to believe in liberty without the NAP?
Can you be a Libertarian without believing in the NAP?
THE NAP is predicated on the Golden Rule which is the motto of the Libertarian party

It depends on what you mean by "libertarian." Some people use it to mean the same thing as Ancap, but I really doubt that's common usage. In America at least, it tends to be used to refer to people who lean to the left and social issues and to the right on economic issues. Under that definition, of course you don't have to be an NAP absolutist (I am one) to be a libertarian. Now to be an anarcho-capitalist...
So how would you do that? I'm having a hard time getting around it.

I'm an ancap, so I have to speculate, but I can imagine an argument somewhat along these lines...

"I believe that, in general, increases in economic, social, and personal freedom promote the well-being of society. However, there are some situations in which it may be necessary to curtail those freedoms, such as to gather money for the public defense or for public roads."

The person who made that argument could be said to be a libertarian, but he couldn't be said to be an ancap. I see it as being kind of like the "a square is a rectangle, but a rectangle isn't necessarily a square" type thing. I see libertarian as being the more general term with fuzzier borders.

That's such an interesting way to focus on things. For me I believe that the push for more freedom economic, social and personal stem from a desire to 'live and let live' and therefore there is no ability for me to separate the NAP from the libertarian. I like to consider the libertarian view as 'anti-coercion' which means anti-coercion for 1 person as much as it does for 1000.

Yes absolutely, the Non Aggression Principle is just one moral philosophy to live by. If the general premise is don't hurt, don't steal and don't kill then they have libertarian views. As for being a libertarian with socioeconomic-political matters that's debatable in what you support. Some libertarians oppose other libertarians.
